topic: The Streaming Ad Bounceback vs Doom
description: A timeline comparison of how ad-supported streaming climbed after the 2022 ad squeeze—while linear TV and some streaming ad buyers struggled during the CPM crash, then re-learned the playbook.
youtube_description:
🎬 In this chart-race video, we track the money: streaming video ads and CTV rising after a bruising ad-market reset—while linear TV ad spend keeps sliding year after year.

📍 Chapters (timestamps):
00:00 — The setup: streaming ads start climbing, linear’s decline is already underway
00:28 — 2020: pandemic-era viewing boosts connected TV demand
01:07 — 2021: ad dollars follow the screen shift—CTV accelerates
01:45 — 2022: the squeeze hits (CPMs wobble, budgets tighten)
02:22 — 2023: bounceback begins—streaming regains momentum
02:58 — 2024: the new normal—measured, addressable reach wins budgets
03:40 — 2025: consolidation of the playbook—CTV scales faster
04:18 — 2026 (latest projection window): streaming ads and CTV keep pulling forward

📌 What to watch for in the animation:
- Who grows fastest during the “ad reset” years
- The inflection where streaming stops losing share to linear
- The widening gap between connected TV spend and linear TV

instagram_caption:
🚀 The ad money didn’t just move to streaming—it REWROTE the scoreboard.

Back in 2019, US advertisers were still pouring roughly **$70.1B** into **linear TV ads**. Streaming video ads were a smaller lane at **$16.8B**, and CTV sat at **$11.7B**. Then the world flipped.

In **2020**, viewing surged on connected devices, and the ad market followed: **Streaming Video Ads** rose to **$19.6B** and **CTV** hit **$13.8B**, while linear slid to **$64.8B**. By **2021**, streaming had the wind: **Streaming Ads** jumped to **$24.7B** and **CTV** surged to **$18.5B**, as linear continued dropping to **$60.2B**.

But the plot twists in **2022**. Budgets tightened and CPMs wobbled—**Streaming Ads** slipped from **$24.7B to $23.1B**. Linear didn’t recover either, falling further to **$56.7B**. The “doom” part wasn’t about streaming dying—it was about advertisers hitting pause, learning new measurement, and renegotiating expectations.

Then came the bounceback. In **2023**, streaming climbed to **$28.4B** and CTV accelerated to **$27.6B**. By **2024**, **Streaming Ads** reached **$34.9B** while linear fell to **$47.2B**. **2025** keeps pushing: **Streaming Ads $39.8B** and **CTV $38.7B**, while linear drops to **$43.6B**. And in **2026**, the race keeps stretching—**Streaming Ads projected $46.0B** and **CTV projected $44.5B** versus linear at **$40.3B**.

So here’s the real question: when advertisers think “video ads,” do they still picture linear—or do they already think CTV-first? 👇

The US advertising market’s shift from linear TV to streaming isn’t a slow fade—it’s a multi-year reallocation with clear inflection points.

In 2019, linear TV dominated at **$70.1B** in ad spend, while streaming video ads sat at **$16.8B** and CTV at **$11.7B**. During 2020, connected viewing accelerated demand: streaming ads rose to **$19.6B** and CTV increased to **$13.8B**, while linear declined to **$64.8B**. By 2021, advertisers leaned harder into the new screens—streaming reached **$24.7B** and CTV **$18.5B**, as linear fell to **$60.2B**.

The market’s pressure point came in 2022. Streaming video ads dipped to **$23.1B** as budgets tightened, but the decline didn’t reverse the longer-term trend: linear continued sliding to **$56.7B**. Recovery was swift: streaming climbed to **$28.4B** in 2023 and **$34.9B** in 2024. CTV strengthened even faster, reaching **$33.9B** in 2024. By 2025, streaming video ads were **$39.8B** and CTV **$38.7B**, while linear fell to **$43.6B**.

In the latest 2026 outlook, streaming is projected to reach **$46.0B** (streaming video) and **$44.5B** (CTV), while linear continues its downward path to **$40.3B**—a widening gap that reflects not just audience migration, but advertiser confidence in addressable measurement.

Which will you watch in the next cycle: CPM stability in CTV or linear’s attempted comeback?
